newsitem.title: USA: Clinton and Kohl discuss NATO, Yeltsin summit.
newsitem.headline: Clinton and Kohl discuss NATO, Yeltsin summit.

text.p: President Bill Clinton and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl spoke by telephone for about 20 minutes on Wednesday, covering the expansion of the NATO Western alliance and other issues, the White House said.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters the two also discussed Clinton's March 20-21 Helsinki summit meeting with Russian President Boris Yeltsin and the issue of economic cooperation with Russia.
One of the key topics expected to arise in Helsinki is the enlargement of NATO, the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation, which Russia has resisted.
The alliance is expected at its Madrid summit in July to invite several countries -- probably Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic -- to join NATO by 1999.
